name: extract
oneLiner: URL to structured JSON, with a parser ladder that tells you when it gave up.
description: A FastAPI service that turns arbitrary URLs into structured JSON. It falls back through trafilatura, then Playwright for JS-heavy pages, then readability, then selectolax, and returns 422 rather than silently handing back a bot wall as if it were an article. Every extraction ships a weighted confidence score instead of a boolean, and an SSRF gate blocks hosts that resolve to both a public and a private address — because you don't control which one the OS picks.

name: QuickSign
oneLiner: In-browser ASL learning game, verifying signs on-device.
description: An in-browser American Sign Language learning game, co-founded with Abdur Rafay Khan. Recognition runs entirely on-device with MediaPipe hand landmarks feeding a Bi-GRU model trained on a custom dataset — the camera feed never leaves the device. The model is a veto-only layer: it can reject a sign as wrong but never unilaterally approve one. It was rebuilt around a rolling ~2-second movement window after an earlier version scored a static, motionless hand shape as a correct sign for "coffee" — that class of false positive is now structurally prevented.
note: Built in collaboration — no public repo under my account.

name: Ledger
oneLiner: Bilingual EN/اردو bookkeeping for a heavy-equipment rental business.
description: A single-file, no-build-step, no-dependency bookkeeping and invoicing tool for tracking rental machines, clients, and payments — in English and Urdu, properly right-to-left, not a translated string table bolted onto a left-to-right design. Data is encrypted client-side with WebCrypto AES-GCM 256 and a PBKDF2-derived key, stored in localStorage. The 6-digit PIN is deliberately excluded from protecting the cloud copy: it's offline-brute-forcible in about two minutes, and pretending otherwise would be worse than saying so.

name: DineSync
oneLiner: Restaurant reservations, built to run on both a Windows dev box and Linux serverless.
description: A restaurant table-reservation system with a dual database backend: SQL Server locally through the Windows-only msnodesqlv8 ODBC driver, and Postgres in production — the only one of the two that runs inside a Linux serverless function. That split is the actual engineering decision here, not a stack choice made for its own sake.
